evidence: Cic. Mil. 65: vulnus quod acū pūnctum vidērētur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The plain word for pricking with a point: a needle, a thorn, the tines of a fork. Of pricking pastry all over before it goes in the oven, with furcillā and passim; see the examples.

phrases.latin: Solum furcillā passim punge, nē in furnō intumēscat.
phrases.english: Prick the base all over with a fork, so that it doesn’t puff up in the oven.

phrases.latin: Ūnum laganum fistulā percutiēs, in superficiem pōnēs.
phrases.english: Prick one sheet of pastry with a reed and lay it on top.

sources: Lewis & Short: pungo · Lewis & Short: compungo · Lewis & Short: percutio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 362.
